page.description: Batocera.linux editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A Buildroot-based retro-gaming system that boots straight into EmulationStation, published as ready-made disk images per board and CPU class.
pros: Ready-made image: write it to a stick and boot into EmulationStation.
Hundreds of emulators and cores are set up out of the box.
The userdata partition holds ROMs and saves and survives a reflash.
Kodi is built in for media playback.
cons: Not a general-purpose desktop: the front-end is the system.
One image per board and CPU class, so picking the right file matters.
The 32-bit x86 build is a 2021 release and is not pinned here.
The publisher states no support window for a release.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Batocera.linux; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the .img.gz for your CPU class to a USB stick with an image writer; writing erases the whole device. On first boot the system expands its userdata partition and reboots, and must not be interrupted.
